timing.note: Spins up with an 80 ms time constant (the dc-motor model); flow follows the impeller speed with no water inertia or priming delay.

analog.note: Brushed DC motor: winding resistance from 4× the running current, back-EMF, friction (the dc-motor model). Flow is linear in speed above 20 % of the rated speed and is the free-flow (no lift) figure; real flow drops with every centimetre of lift and tube length.

power.note: Running and start-up current are realistic, so relay, driver and GPIO checks apply. Running dry is not detected.

emulates: Flow vs voltage and PWM duty
doesNotEmulate: Lift (head) and tube length, which reduce flow a lot
Priming: a pump above the water line pumps nothing
Electrical noise that resets boards without a flyback diode and a capacitor
testOnRealDevice: Measure millilitres per second with your tube and lift, then set flowLph so pumpedMl matches
Keep it submerged; never run it dry
Put a diode across the pump (cathode to +) and a 100 µF capacitor on the supply
